blocks: The FCC fined one man one hundred twenty million dollars, without counting the calls.
The FCC says Adrian Abramovich was behind ninety-six million robocalls, in just three months.
Instead of counting them all, the FCC sampled eighty thousand. About a thousand for each day.
Each sampled call counted as one thousand dollars. That is eighty million. Then it added forty million more. One hundred twenty million.
And every one of those eighty thousand sampled calls used a spoofed number.
His defense? No one is harmed unless they answer, and stay on the line for about five minutes. The FCC ruled that what matters is intent, not proof of harm on every call.
Chairman Ajit Pai called it the largest fine in the agency's history. The full case, and the law that came next, is on The Rule Changed.
